name: TFM-4AS-1

lead: TFM-4AS-1 is a steroidal SARM that muscle-building readers cite for adding muscle and bone while having smaller effects on reproductive organs and oil-producing skin glands in rats.

It partially activates the androgen receptor and blocks the receptor's internal N/C-terminal interaction, so only some androgen-responsive genes switch on. A 2009 Journal of Biological Chemistry study found ovariectomized rats gained bone and muscle mass without prostate growth. No human study exists.

paras: It is a laboratory compound with no established routine. Any physique use is discussed from the rat work.
Human safety is unknown. It is not approved for any use.

angle.text: TFM-4AS-1 is a steroidal SARM that muscle-building readers cite for adding muscle and bone while sparing reproductive tissue in rats. It partially activates the androgen receptor, switching on only some androgen-responsive genes. Research is limited to laboratory work.

lead: TFM-4AS-1 is an experimental steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) described in a 2009 paper in the Journal of Biological Chemistry. It belongs to the 4-aza-steroid class and was characterised as a potent androgen receptor ligand that only partially activates the receptor [1]. The appearance interest is the SARM idea: building muscle and bone, the basis of a fuller physique, while sparing reproductive tissue and skin oil glands, which are linked to acne and oily skin.

In that study, ovariectomized rats given TFM-4AS-1 gained bone and muscle mass with reduced effects on reproductive organs and sebaceous glands, and the compound did not promote prostate growth [1]. Wikipedia describes it as an abandoned investigational compound that also inhibits 5-alpha-reductase [2]. No human studies of TFM-4AS-1 have been published, and it has no approved use.
SARMs as a class are investigational; as of 2023 neither the FDA nor the EMA had approved one, and they are sought by some bodybuilders and banned in sport by WADA [3].

paras: The authors reported that TFM-4AS-1 binds the androgen receptor with an IC50 of 38 nM, activates an androgen-dependent promoter to about 55 percent of the maximal response, and antagonizes the interaction between the receptor's N- and C-terminal regions needed for full activation [1]. Gene-expression analysis in a breast cancer cell line showed it induced some androgen-responsive genes as strongly as dihydrotestosterone and others weakly or not at all, which the authors proposed as a basis for tissue selectivity [1]. They compared it with a closely related full agonist, Cl-4AS-1 [1]. A later modelling study used TFM-4AS-1 as an example of a partial agonist, which acts as an agonist at low effect levels and an antagonist at high levels when combined with a full agonist [4].
An in vitro study of four SARMs, including TFM-4AS-1, mapped metabolic pathways such as hydroxylation, demethylation and glucuronidation as potential markers for doping control [5].

No studies found in humans. In preclinical work, ovariectomized rats treated with TFM-4AS-1 accrued bone and muscle with reduced effects on reproductive tissues and sebaceous glands compared with the full agonist [1].

TFM-4AS-1 is among the compounds included in analytical methods for detecting SARMs in urine, and SARMs in general are monitored in anti-doping testing [6][3][5]. Wikipedia reports that bodybuilders use SARMs, that much of the online market is gray-market and that one study found most products sold as SARMs were mislabeled [3]. No source documents use of TFM-4AS-1 in looksmaxxing communities.
